title: Jonah and the Echo
premise: Cyrus Kavanagh, the last caretaker of the Svalgard Seed Vault, has spent eleven years alone recording the slow collapse of a colony Earth abandoned after the Meridian War cut off all contact. When a distress signal arrives in Old Terran—a language extinct for two centuries—Cyrus decodes it and learns the vault holds a sealed archive: proof that Earth's government, not the colonies, fired first. Delivering that message could end the war, but both sides would rather destroy the evidence, and a hunter-ship is already inbound. In the end, Cyrus broadcasts the truth in every dead language at once, sacrificing the vault and their own recorded identity so the echo outlives them.
about_author: August Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete media formats before turning to fiction. They write quiet, melancholy science fiction about the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Long Inventory
chapters.summary: Cyrus Kavanagh's POV. A routine day cataloguing seeds in the vast, frozen vault establishes Cyrus's rituals, loneliness, and the daily log they record for an audience that stopped listening years ago. The emotional beat is tender resignation—the comfort of routine masking grief.

chapters.title: Eleven Winters
chapters.summary: Cyrus reviews old logs from previous caretakers, tracing how supply ships dwindled to nothing after the Meridian War began. Flashbacks reveal why Cyrus volunteered: a sister lost on a colony ship. The beat is quiet sorrow and stubborn duty.

chapters.title: A Sound Like Breathing
chapters.summary: During a solar storm, the vault's ancient array picks up a repeating signal—not in any code Cyrus knows. POV stays with Cyrus as wonder cracks open the monotony. The beat is trembling hope, quickly shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Old Terran
chapters.summary: Cyrus digs into the vault's linguistic archives and identifies the signal's language: Old Terran, extinct since the Reformation of Tongues two centuries ago. Someone is deliberately speaking to the past. The beat is intellectual thrill laced with dread.

chapters.title: The Sealed Wing
chapters.summary: Following coordinates embedded in the signal, Cyrus breaches a wing of the vault even the caretaker manuals redact. Inside: a transmission array and a locked archive stamped with Earth Directorate seals. The beat is transgressive awe—Cyrus crossing a line.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Cyrus decrypts fragments: fleet telemetry, casualty figures, and a discrepancy suggesting the war's official origin story is false. POV alternates briefly with the signal's sender, Vess, a colonial linguist broadcasting blind. The beat is dawning horror.

chapters.title: Vess
chapters.summary: Full POV shift to Vess aboard the colony ship Perennial, hiding from her own government while transmitting in a dead tongue because dead tongues can't be censored. She doesn't know if anyone hears. The beat is desperate faith.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Frequency
chapters.summary: Cyrus answers the signal. Vess receives confirmation that someone exists—and that the archive she's been seeking is real. Their halting exchange across light-years forms an unlikely bond. The beat is cautious intimacy between strangers.

chapters.title: The Hunter's Wake
chapters.summary: Cyrus detects a ship decelerating toward the vault: the Directorate retrieval vessel Charybdis, flagged for 'heritage asset recovery.' Both know what recovery means. The beat is cold fear tightening around fragile purpose.

chapters.title: Deniability
chapters.summary: The Charybdis hails the vault with scripted courtesy; its captain, Ilsa Reyen, probes Cyrus's knowledge in conversation that reads like an interrogation. Cyrus lies badly, then learns to lie well. The beat is the corruption of innocence under pressure.

chapters.title: Archive of Ashes
chapters.summary: Cyrus finishes decrypting the core file: launch records proving Earth fired the first shot and let the colonies be blamed. The weight of it nearly breaks them. The beat is vertigo—truth as a burden rather than a gift.

chapters.title: Reyen's Offer
chapters.summary: Captain Reyen boards under pretext of inspection and privately offers Cyrus extraction, wealth, a life off-world—in exchange for the archive's destruction. She reveals she's read his logs; she knows his loneliness. The beat is temptation aimed precisely at a wound.

chapters.title: The Log Nobody Asked For
chapters.summary: Alone again, Cyrus listens back through eleven years of recordings and confronts who they've become: a witness, or a coward with a microphone. Vess urges broadcast before the Charybdis can jam the array. The beat is painful self-recognition.

chapters.title: Sabotage in Slow Motion
chapters.summary: Cyrus begins covertly rerouting power to the deep-space transmitter, sabotaging the vault's own containment systems. Reyen grows suspicious as systems flicker. The beat is escalating tension, each small act irreversible.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Cold
chapters.summary: Reyen catches Cyrus mid-sabotage. Instead of arresting him, she confesses: her orders are to erase the vault entirely, crew included, and she's looking for a reason to refuse. The beat is unexpected alliance born of shared complicity.

chapters.title: The Countdown
chapters.summary: The Charybdis's political officer discovers the mutiny brewing and locks down the ship, moving to destroy the archive early. Vess's colony ship, pursued by colonial hardliners, may not reach relay range in time. The beat is the trap closing from all sides.

chapters.title: Every Dead Language
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Cyrus initiates the broadcast, encoding the truth in Old Terran, pre-Reformation dialects, and seed-catalog cipher simultaneously—languages no censor can fully suppress. Reyen's crew buys minutes with a staged malfunction. The beat is defiant exhilaration.

chapters.title: Charybdis Ascending
chapters.summary: The political officer fires on the vault's transmitter array. Cyrus, wounded, keeps the broadcast alive by hand-wiring the backup dish in the storm as Reyen turns her own guns on her bridge. The beat is sacrifice amid chaos.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: The message reaches the Perennial and, through Vess's relay network, a hundred colonial receivers—and, unexpectedly, sympathetic ears inside Earth itself. The war's founding lie becomes common knowledge faster than either government can contain it. The beat is release after long compression.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Ceasefire talks convene under public pressure no faction can ignore. Reyen, court-martialed, testifies; Vess becomes an unwilling symbol. Cyrus, presumed dead in the vault's collapse, watches the news feeds from a hidden shelter. The beat is bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: The Gardener's Grave
chapters.summary: Cyrus returns to the ruined vault one last time, salvaging a single case of seeds and the complete log of eleven years. They plant nothing yet—they carry it instead, toward the colonies, toward Vess. The beat is mourning transformed into forward motion.

chapters.title: New Tongue
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating Cyrus and Vess POV as they meet at last on the Perennial. Cyrus records a new first entry—for a future audience this time—and the seeds are sown in colonial soil. The beat is quiet renewal: memory preserved, identity chosen, power returned to the many.
